annotation.summary_en: A businessman returns from abroad to find his secretary reporting a series of catastrophic business failures, only to end on a surprising personal note.
annotation.summary_detailed_en: The sketch opens in a bright office corridor where Mr. Gharibyan, a mustachioed manager in a grey suit, returns from a trip abroad. He settles at his desk in a private office equipped with a CRT monitor and a fax machine. His secretary, a woman with curly hair wearing a black turtleneck, is initially seen working in the outer office before entering his room with papers. As Mr. Gharibyan sips a small cup of coffee and asks for news, the secretary delivers an increasingly intense and wide-eyed rant in extreme close-up. She lists a series of disasters: the factory was raided and fined 1.5 million dollars, their German partners cancelled their contracts leading to a lawsuit in Berlin, the bank is auctioning his villa and cars due to loan defaults, and bald men in black jackets have threatened a hostile takeover within two hours. The tension is punctuated by intercut illustrations of a commando with a rifle. When the stunned boss asks if there is any good news from the last ten days, the secretary smiles and reveals the punchline: they are going to have a baby.
